aspects.says: BigDecimal and BigInteger are not final, so a kept instance from untrusted code may be a mutable subclass.
basis: section:An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection

aspects.says: A constructor checks every argument before it stores or hands out `this`, so a refused object is never reachable.
basis: section:A Constructor That Fails Has Already Published this If It Registered Itself First

aspects.says: A final field holds a reference; a class is immutable only as deep as its copy, so mutable elements are copied too or replaced by immutable ones.
basis: section:An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection

aspects.says: Deserializing a Serializable class runs only the no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass, so readObject repeats the constructor's checks after defaultReadObject and throws InvalidObjectException.
basis: section:Deserialization Builds the Object Without Your Constructor, So readObject Checks Again

aspects.says: A class whose fields are all final gets the final-field publication guarantee.
basis: section:An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection
aspects.reason: stated with a pointer to unit 5.2.2; visibility under a data race can't be shown deterministically by a graded test

aspects.says: Final fields and no setters don't make a type immutable while it can be subclassed; the class is final, or has only private constructors.
basis: section:An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection

aspects.says: A serializable singleton deserializes to a second instance unless readResolve returns the existing one.
basis: section:Deserialization Builds the Object Without Your Constructor, So readObject Checks Again
aspects.reason: a one-sentence side note on the page; the unit's practices stay on validation

aspects.says: A record is deserialized through its canonical constructor, so its checks run on the stream's values.
basis: section:Deserialization Builds the Object Without Your Constructor, So readObject Checks Again

aspects.says: An exception from a constructor only keeps `new` from returning a reference; a reference the constructor already handed out survives, with unassigned fields at their defaults.
basis: section:A Constructor That Fails Has Already Published this If It Registered Itself First

aspects.says: setAccessible(true) lets Field.set write a non-static final field of an ordinary class, but not of a record, a hidden class or a static final field.
basis: section:Reflection Can Rewrite a private final Field of a Class, but Not of a Record
